history.dynasty: Kalachuri (c. 975 CE, attributed by Krishna Deva; agreed by Dhirendra Singh)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is NOT in Satna town - it stands in MAIHAR, which was separated from Satna as its own district in 2023. Golamath (Gola Math) is an east-facing Shiva temple on a platform following a pancharatha (five-projection) plan with a panchanga (five-part) elevation in the Nagara order: garbhagrha, antarala and mukha-mandapa, with a ten-storey latina-style shikhara. The pitha has multiple mouldings topped by a grasa-pattika; the vedibandha has kumbha, kalasa and kumuda mouldings; the two-tier jangha carries sculptures (large below, small above) with ashta-dikpalas on the karna-rathas and surasundaris on the prati-rathas; the bhadra niches hold Shiva-Andhakantaka, Durga (Chamunda), Kartikeya and Parvati, with Surya over the kumbha. The five-shakha antarala doorway shows Shiva on the lalata-bimba flanked by Brahma, Vishnu, the Navagrahas, Sapta-matrikas, Shiva-Vinadhara, Ganesha and Shaiva dvarapalas. With no inscription, it is dated by style to ~975 CE, Kalachuri. It is a state-protected monument, standing on Deviji Road opposite Bara Akhara, Maihar.

name: Golamath Temple
town: Maihar, Maihar district (CSV town 'Satna' is WRONG - the temple is in Maihar city, headquarters of the new Maihar district carved out of Satna in 2023)
town_description: Maihar is the headquarters of Maihar district in the Vindhya region, famous for the Maa Sharada Temple (Shaktipeeth) on Trikuta hill and as the home of the Maihar Gharana of Indian classical music (Allauddin Khan, Ravi Shankar, Ali Akbar Khan). A railway station on the Howrah-Mumbai line; about 40 km from Satna.
